newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli soldiers wound two Palestinians in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israeli soldiers wound two Palestinians in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli troops firing rubber bullets wounded two Palestinians on Tuesday in the fourth straight day of clashes in the divided West Bank town of Hebron, witnesses said.
They said several dozen youths began throwing stones in the area of a fortified Jewish settler enclave in the heart of the town.

Soldiers immediately deployed opposite the demonstrators and on surrounding roofs. They initially withheld fire but when one youth set a large Israeli flag on fire and danced in front of them they opened fire, wounding the youth in the leg.
In a second incident, an elderly Palestinian was struck in the forehead by a rubber bullet as he passed the site of the clashes, the witnesses said.
The army said it was checking the reports.
Both wounded Palestinians were dragged to the rear of the clashes where ambulances stood waiting and Palestinian medical personnel had set up a small treatment area.

The violence underscored rising Israel-PLO tensions over a three-month deadlock in peace efforts and what Palestinians view as an Israeli drive to expand Jewish settlements in the Gaza Strip and Jerusalem and the rest of the West Bank.
On Monday, soldiers shot and wounded at least 38 Palestinians in clashes at the town.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused the Palestinian Authority on Monday of ordering violence in Gaza and of doing nothing to stop unrest in Hebron.

"There was a clear set of instructions a few days ago in Gaza for the violence that took place there," Netanyahu told reporters after he addressed a parliamentary committee in Jerusalem, referring to unrest last week.
"I can't tell you about Hebron in the last 24 hours because I haven't seen the reports. But I can tell you that the Palestinian police have refrained from acting against the violence," he said.

Israel handed 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian rule under an interim peace deal in January but kept troops at the heart of the town to protect some 400 Jewish settlers who live there in fortified enclaves.
